COMPTROLLER’S DECISION

This decision is considered final on 01/29/2024, unless a motion for rehearing is timely filed; this date of finality is calculated based on the Administrative Procedure Act (APA). [ENDNOTE 1] The failure to timely file a motion for rehearing may result in adverse legal consequences.

Administrative Law Judge (ALJ) Kathy Pickup of the State Office of Administrative Hearings (SOAH) issued a Proposal for Decision (PFD) that includes Findings of Fact and Conclusions of Law. SOAH served the PFD on each party and each party was given an opportunity to file exceptions and replies with SOAH in accordance with SOAH’s rules of procedure. The ALJ recommended that the Comptroller adopt the PFD as written.

After review and consideration, IT IS ORDERED that the PFD is adopted as written.

The result from this Decision is Attachment A. The ALJ’s recommendation letter is Attachment B. The PFD as written is Attachment C. Attachments A, B, and C are incorporated by reference.

Attachment A reflects a liability.

SIGNED on this 4th day of January 2024

GLENN HEGAR

Comptroller of Public Accounts

By: Lisa Craven

Deputy Comptroller

ATTACHMENT C

SOAH Docket No. 304-24-01983.88

Before the State Office of Administrative Hearings

TCPA Hearing No. 119,949

Proposal for Decision

The The Criminal Investigation Division (CID) of the Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts (Comptroller) determined that **************, dba **************, (Petitioner) violated statutory regulation by failing to display a proper tobacco warning sign. On July 6, 2023, the CID issued a Notice of Violation No. ************** for Cigarette/Tobacco Retailer Permit No. ************** (Tobacco Permit), held by Petitioner, imposing a $1,000 fine authorized under the Texas Health and Safety Code. [ENDNOTE 2] Petitioner requested a hearing to dispute the imposition of the fine. In this Proposal for Decision, the Administrative Law Judge (ALJ) recommends the fine proposed by the Tax Division (Staff) of the Comptroller be imposed.

I. NOTICE, JURISDICTION, AND PROCEDURAL HISTORY

Staff referred this case to the State Office of Administrative Hearings (SOAH) and, on September 29, 2023, issued its Notice of Hearing by Written Submission to Petitioner. On October 4, 2023, ALJ Kathy Pickup issued an Order Setting Written Submission Requirements. Teresa Gutierrez represented Staff, and Petitioner was represented by **************. The contested case record closed on December 11, 2023.

There are no issues of notice or jurisdiction; therefore, those matters are set out in the Findings of Fact and Conclusions of Law without further discussion.

II. REASONS FOR DECISION

A. EVIDENCE

Petitioner did not submit evidence for the hearing. Staff offered the following exhibits:

Notice of Violation;

Texas Comptroller Form 69-401, Cigarette Inspection Report;

Texas Comptroller Criminal Investigative Report, Case No. **************; and

Photographs of Petitioner’s Premises.

Staff’s exhibits were admitted without objection.

B. MATERIAL FACTS AND ISSUES PRESENTED

Petitioner operates a convenience store at ADDRESS, CITY, Texas. Petitioner is a tobacco retailer and sells cigarettes and other tobacco products under its tobacco permit, issued by the Comptroller. On June 22, 2023, Investigator Daniel Doss, a State Police Investigator commissioned by the Comptroller’s CID, conducted a tobacco inspection in accordance with Texas Tax Code §§ 154.304 and 155.210 and Texas Health and Safety Code §§ 161.088 and 147.0051(b).

Officer Doss visited Petitioner’s business and conducted surveillance and determined the business was open and operational. Officer Doss entered the premises and conducted a tobacco inspection of the business. He did not observe a warning “No one under 21 permitted” sign printed on the front door, nor did he observe the mandatory Tobacco/Cigarette Warning sign posted in a manner that was in view of the public and clerks from the point of sale for tobacco products.

On July 6, 2023, CID issued a formal Notice of Violation (Notice) ************** regarding Permit No. **************, held by Petitioner, citing failure to display proper warning sign in violation of Chapter 161 of the Health and Safety Code. The Notice stated the Comptroller intended to impose a fine of up to $1,000 on Petitioner for the violation and provided Petitioner the opportunity to request a hearing on the matter.

On July 13, 2023, Petitioner returned the respective form, indicating it wanted a hearing. On August 17, 2023, Staff referred the matter to SOAH and issued its Notice of Hearing by Written Submission to Petitioner on September 29, 2023. Staff maintains that the proposed fine for the violations should be upheld. Petitioner did not submit argument or evidence for the written submission hearing.

C. ALJ ANALYSIS AND RECOMMENDATION

Staff is alleging statutory violations that warrant imposition of a penalty or other disciplinary action and must establish the violations by a preponderance of the evidence. See 34 Tex. Admin. Code § 3.1204(g). Texas issues permits to several types of tobacco dealers. A tobacco permit holder is defined as a bonded agent, distributor, wholesaler, manufacturer, importer, export warehouse, or retailer who obtains a permit under Texas Tax Code § 154.101. See Tex. Tax Code § 154.001(14). A tobacco retailer is defined as a person who engages in the business of selling cigarettes to consumers and includes the owner of a cigarette vending machine. See id. § 154.001(17). In this case, there is no dispute regarding the fact that Petitioner was a tobacco retailer and held a tobacco permit at the time of the violations at issue.

If the Comptroller finds, after notice and an opportunity for a hearing as provided by Texas Government Code Chapter 2001, that a permit holder has violated Texas Health and Safety Code Chapter 161 at a place of business for which a permit is issued, the Comptroller may suspend the permit for that place of business and administratively assess a fine. See id. § 161.0901(b). For the first violation during the 24-month period preceding the violation at that place of business, the Comptroller may require the permit holder to pay a fine in an amount not to exceed $1,000. See id. § 161.0901(b)(1). The statutory scheme imposes strict liability, so that if the agent or employee of the retailer is found to have committed an offense under Chapter 161, the retailer is liable for sanctions noticed under § 161.0901.

Texas Health and Safety Code § 161.084(a) requires that each person who sells cigarettes, ecigarettes, or tobacco products at retail or by vending machine post a sign in a conspicuous location and close to the place where these products may be purchased. The sign must include the statement detailed in Texas Health and Safety Code § 161.084(b). In his Investigation Report, Officer Doss stated that he did not observe the proper warning signs posted in view of the public and employees from the point of sale for tobacco products. Petitioner failed to present evidence to the contrary, therefore, the ALJ recommends that the fine for the violation be upheld.

III. FINDINGS OF FACT

**************, dba **************, (Petitioner) operates a convenience store at ADDRESS, CITY Texas.

Petitioner is a tobacco retailer and sells cigarettes and other tobacco products under its tobacco permit, issued by the Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts (Comptroller).

There is no dispute regarding the fact that Petitioner was a tobacco retailer and held a tobacco permit at the time of the violations at issue.

On June 22, 2023, Investigator Daniel Doss, a State Police Investigator commissioned by the Comptroller’s Criminal Investigation Division (CID), conducted a tobacco inspection in accordance with Texas Tax Code §§ 154.304 and 155.210 and Texas Health and Safety Code §§ 161.088 and 147.0051(b).

Officer Doss visited Petitioner’s business and conducted surveillance and determined the business was open and operational.

Officer Doss did not observe a warning “No one under 21 permitted” sign printed on the front door, nor did he observe the mandatory Tobacco/Cigarette Warning sign posted in a manner that was in view of the public and clerks from the point of sale for tobacco products.

On July 6, 2023, CID issued a formal Notice of Violation (Notice) ************** regarding Permit No. **************, held by Petitioner, citing failure to display proper warning sign in violation of Chapter 161 of the Health and Safety Code.

The Notice stated the Tax Division (Staff) of the Comptroller intended to impose a fine of up to $1,000 on Petitioner for the violation and provided Petitioner the opportunity to request a hearing on the matter.

On July 13, 2023, Petitioner returned the respective form, indicating it wanted a hearing.

On August 17, 2023, Staff referred the matter to SOAH and issued its Notice of Hearing by Written Submission to Petitioner on September 29, 2023. The notice contained a statement of the nature of the hearing; a statement of the legal authority and jurisdiction under which the hearing was to be held; a reference to the particular sections of the statutes and rules involved; and a short, plain statement of the factual matters asserted, or an attachment that incorporated by reference the factual matters asserted in the complaint or petition filed with the state agency.

On October 4, 2023, Administrative Law Judge Kathy Pickup issued an Order Setting Written Submission Requirements.

Petitioner did not submit evidence for the hearing.

The contested case record closed on December 11, 2023.

CONCLUSIONS OF LAW

The Comptroller has jurisdiction over these matters. See Tex. Tax Code ch. 111.

SOAH has jurisdiction over matters related to the hearing, including the authority to issue a proposal for decision with findings of fact and conclusions of law. See Tex. Gov’t Code ch. 2003.

Staff provided a proper and timely notice of hearing. See Tex. Gov’t Code ch. 2001; Tex. Health and Safety Code § 161.0901.

Staff is alleging statutory violations that warrant imposition of a penalty or other disciplinary action and must establish the violations by a preponderance of the evidence. See 34 Tex. Admin. Code § 3.1204(g).

Texas issues permits to several types of tobacco dealers. A tobacco permit holder is defined as a bonded agent, distributor, wholesaler, manufacturer, importer, export warehouse, or retailer who obtains a permit under Texas Tax Code § 154.101. See Tex. Tax Code § 154.001(14).

A tobacco retailer is defined as a person who engages in the business of selling cigarettes to consumers and includes the owner of a cigarette vending machine. See Tex. Tax Code § 154.001(17).

If the Comptroller finds, after notice and an opportunity for a hearing as provided by Texas Government Code Chapter 2001, that a permit holder has violated Texas Health and Safety Code Chapter 161 at a place of business for which a permit is issued, the Comptroller may suspend the permit for that place of business and administratively assess a fine. See Tex. Health and Safety Code § 161.0901(b).

For the first violation during the 24-month period preceding the violation at that place of business, the Comptroller may require the permit holder to pay a fine in an amount not to exceed $1,000. See Tex. Health and Safety Code § 161.0901(b)(1).

Texas Health and Safety Code § 161.084(a) requires that each person who sells cigarettes, e-cigarettes, or tobacco products at retail or by vending machine post a sign in a conspicuous location and close to the place where these products may be purchased.

The sign must include the statement detailed in Texas Health and Safety Code § 161.084(b).

The record evidence supports the finding that the proper warning signs were not posted in view of the public and employees from the point of sale for tobacco products.

Petitioner failed to meet its evidentiary burden to establish that the fine should not be imposed.

The ALJ recommends that the fine for this violation be upheld.

Signed December 12, 2023

Kathy Pickup

Presiding Administrative Law Judge
